claims.text: HEA coatings on transition-metal matrices exhibit non-monotonic tribological performance as ambient temperature rises.
Tribological performance initially improves with increasing temperature up to a critical threshold.
The initial improvement is caused by thermally activated solid-solution strengthening and strain-rate sensitivity.
Above the critical temperature, thermal softening and oxidative wear rapidly degrade performance.
Al0.6TiCrFeCoNi coating can be deposited on ASTM A572 steel by HVOF thermal spraying.
CoCrFeMnNi-based coatings can be formed on a steel transition-metal matrix by cladding.
The proposed coatings possess a dual-phase BCC/FCC or ceramic/matrix microstructure.
Enhanced configurational entropy can stabilize a solid-solution or single-phase HEA structure.
At moderate temperatures, entropy-stabilized solid solutions enhance strain hardening and delay plastic deformation.
At sufficiently high temperature, dynamic recovery or recrystallization softens the coating.
The FCC phase of CoCrFeMnNi is readily deformed.
High-temperature oxidation produces brittle oxide scales that spall under sliding shear and accelerate wear.
Wear rate decreases as temperature rises from 300 K to approximately 500-600 K.
Wear rate increases sharply above approximately 600-700 K.
For Al-containing HEAs, the degradation boundary is between 600 K and 700 K.
The degradation boundary occurs when significant yield-strength loss coincides with the formation of unstable, spall-prone oxide scales.
The cited evidence suggests improved performance over 300-500 °C.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome places initial improvement only up to about 500-600 K and degradation above 600-700 K, whereas the uncertainty field says the evidence suggests improvement from 300-500 °C (573-773 K). That Celsius range overlaps and extends beyond the proposed degradation boundary.
